Subject: Triton private deployment — split-plane runtime routing & observability handshake

Hi Alice / Raj,

Thanks for carving out time this week. Attached is the reference pack we promised: a narrated controlplane/data-plane split diagram, a draw.io export showing routing and NAT demarcation, and a first-draft observability runbook. High-level points we want to align on:

- Control plane (managed by Redwood Private) remains in the customer VPC control subnet; data-plane (inference GPUs) stays in their on-prem pod with an egress gateway.
- We recommend a TLS-terminated mTLS tunnel for control messages (controlplane -> runtime agent) and a separate TLS overlay for data-plane telemetry to avoid cross-contamination of keys.
- BGP is optional for large colo installs; for Triton pilot we propose static routes + a simple NAT at the demarc.
- Observability: we will ship tokenized tracing headers to your Splunk/Datadog proxy — no raw logs leave the pod unless you opt in.

Requests from our side before the design review on Thursday:
1) Confirm whether Triton wants BGP advertised service IPs or if static routes are preferred for the pilot.
2) Any enforced egress port blocks (we currently use 443 and 5222 for control heartbeats).
3) Who will own the certs and KMS for the cluster (Triton KMS or Redwood-managed keys)?

I've CC'd Jonas and Kimberly from our infra team; Marcus added a short note about KV cache separation in the diagram.

Attachments: vpc-splitplane-reference-diagram.pdf (8 pages), controlplane-dataflow.drawio.png (1), observability-runbook-v1.md (stub)

Cheers,
Naomi Feldman

Subject: Re: Triton private deployment — split-plane runtime routing & observability handshake

Thanks Naomi — the docs look good. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- For the pilot (single rack colo), we'll start with static routes and a NAT at the demarc. We may revisit BGP in phase II.
- Egress policy: security team blocks outbound except 443, 22 to our jump host, and a few control ports; 5222 will need a formal exception. I'll open a policy ticket today.
- Certs: Triton prefers to manage certs via our internal PKI; we can provide a signed leaf cert. For any HSM/KMS-level secrets we may ask Redwood to use customer KMS keys.

Two questions:
1) You mentioned telemetry tokens — is there a way to redact request bodies before they leave the pod?
2) What failure mode do you recommend if the controlplane loses connectivity to the runtime for >2m?

- Alice (on behalf of Triton infra)
Alice Gupta
VP, Infrastructure
Triton Financial

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Triton private deployment — split-plane runtime routing & observability handshake

Naomi — quick internal notes before the call:

On telemetry redaction: we support pre-export filters in the runtime agent. We can configure field-level redaction rules (e.g., strip prompt text bodies) and only export token-level telemetry plus timing/health metrics. That satisfies most compliance requirements. I'll attach a sample filter policy to the Drive link.

On control loss failure mode: for >2m we run a local degraded-mode policy on the runtime:
- Continue serving from last accepted model snapshot for N minutes (configurable).
- Reject new model rollouts until controlplane reconnects.
- Emit an elevated incident to both Triton NOC and Redwood Ops with a guaranteed 1-minute polling cadence.

Also: Marcus flagged a KV-cache boundary concern — we should ensure tenant encryption keys are customer-managed for Triton.

- Jonas
